newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes mostly lower in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes mostly lower in choppy trade.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mostly lower in choppy trade reflecting the current volatility of CBOT soybeans, floor sources said.
"We were a follower market and went back and forth with CBOT soybeans. Forecasts for moisture in hard red (winter wheat) country were also bearish," one floor source said.
They said Prudential Securities and Term Commodities were featured sellers with buying scattered.
Losses were limited by USDA's weekly export report, which said U.S. net wheat exports for the week ended March 6 totaled 355,400 tonnes, slightly higher than expected.
"It (the report) was almost bullish but it wasn't enough to stem the tide," one floor source said.
The thinly-traded spot March contract ended one cent a bushel higher at $4.40 a bushel with the key May position down two cents at $4.08-1/2.
Other months were down 1/2 to 2-1/2 cents.
